column1: improvise§She improvised a splint from two rulers and a scarf.§她用两把尺子和一条围巾**临时做了**个夹板。
imprudent§Imprudent at twenty, cautious at forty, he changed nothing else.§二十岁**轻率**，四十岁谨慎，他其他方面都没变。
impudent§The reply was impudent and, unfortunately, correct.§这个回答**无礼**，可惜是对的。
impugn§Do not impugn the source when you can check the figure.§能核对数字的时候，就别**质疑**出处。
impulsive§An impulsive apology is worth more than a considered one.§**冲动的**道歉比深思熟虑的更有分量。
impute§The historian imputes to them a plan they never had.§这位历史学家把一个他们从未有过的计划**强加于他**们。
inaccessibility§Inaccessibility is why the frescoes survived the war.§正因为**难以到达**，这些壁画才在战争中幸存。
inaccessible§The argument is inaccessible without the second appendix.§没有第二个附录，这个论证**难以理解**。
inaccurate§An inaccurate map is copied more often than a correct one.§一张**不准确**的地图被抄录的次数比正确的更多。
inadequacy§He mistook the inadequacy of the tools for his own.§他把工具的**不足**误当成了自己的不足。
inadequate§Two people were an inadequate crew for a boat that size.§对那么大的船来说，两个人是**不够**的。
inane§An inane question at the right moment can open a discussion.§在对的时刻问一个**愚蠢的**问题，反而能打开讨论。
inappropriate§The word is not wrong, merely inappropriate here.§这个词并没有错，只是在这里**不合适**。
inapt§An inapt title has buried a good article more than once.§**不恰当**的标题不止一次埋没了好文章。
inarticulate§Rage is usually inarticulate and therefore easy to dismiss.§愤怒通常**语无伦次**，因而容易被无视。
inattention§Inattention to the footnotes is how the error spread.§正是对脚注的**疏忽**让错误扩散开来。
inaudible§Below the fourth row the recording is inaudible.§第四排以后，这段录音就**听不见**了。
inauspicious§An inauspicious opening night was followed by a two-year run.§首演之夜**不吉**利，之后却连演了两年。
incandescent§Incandescent bulbs waste most of their energy as heat.§**白炽灯**把大部分能量浪费成了热。
incantatory§The repetition is incantatory rather than emphatic.§这种重复是**咒语**式的，而非强调式的。
incense§Incense hung in the chapel long after the service ended.§礼拜结束很久之后，**香气**还留在礼拜堂里。
inception§From its inception the plan depended on one grant.§**从一开始**，这个计划就依赖一笔资助。
incessant§Incessant revision can be a way of avoiding the ending.§**不停**地修改可能是一种逃避结尾的方式。
inchoate§Inchoate ideas are best kept out of meetings.§**尚未成形**的想法最好别带到会上。
incidental§Incidental music was written for a play nobody now performs.§这些**配乐**是为一出如今无人上演的戏写的。
incisive§An incisive editor cuts and explains why.§**犀利**的编辑既动刀，也解释为什么。
inclination§The inclination of the strata tells you where to dig.§岩层的**倾角**告诉你该在哪里挖。
inclusive§The dates are inclusive: both Mondays count.§这两个日期是**包含**在内的：两个周一都算。
incoherence§Incoherence in a first draft is not a fault; keeping it is.§初稿的**杂乱**不是毛病，保留它才是。
incoherent§Fatigue makes a good writer incoherent by page three.§疲惫让一个好作者到第三页就**语无伦次**。
incompatible§The two schedules are incompatible and both are fixed.§这两份日程互**不相容**，而且都不能改。
incompetent§Calling someone incompetent is easier than reading their file.§说别人**不称职**比读他们的档案容易。
incomprehensible§What is incomprehensible in translation may be plain in the original.§译文里**难以理解**的，原文里可能明白如话。
inconclusive§An inconclusive result is still a result worth publishing.§**没有定论**的结果仍然值得发表。
incongruity§The incongruity is the joke, and it takes a second to land.§**不协调**正是笑点所在，要过一秒才反应过来。
incongruous§Nothing looks more incongruous than a new sign on an old wall.§没有什么比旧墙上的新招牌更**不协调**。
inconsequential§An inconsequential detail can date a document exactly.§一个**无关紧要**的细节可以精确地确定文件年代。
inconsistency§The inconsistency is in the units, not the arithmetic.§**不一致**出在单位上，而不在算术上。
inconsistent§An inconsistent style guide is worse than none.§前后**矛盾的**体例指南比没有还糟。
inconspicuous§The most inconspicuous entry in the ledger was the important one.§账簿里**最不起眼**的那一条才是重要的。
incontrovertible§Nothing here is incontrovertible except the postmark.§除了邮戳，这里没有什么是**无可争辩**的。
incorporate§The town was incorporated in 1873 and renamed twice since.§这个镇于一八七三年**建制**，此后改过两次名。
incorrigible§An incorrigible margin-writer, he ruined every borrowed book.§他是个**改不掉**在页边写字的人，毁了每一本借来的书。
incorruptible§No system is incorruptible; some are merely inconvenient.§没有制度是**不可腐蚀**的，有些只是不方便腐蚀。
incredulous§The incredulous silence lasted longer than the announcement.§**难以置信**的沉默比公告本身还长。
incubate§Eggs incubate for twenty-one days at a steady temperature.§蛋在恒温下**孵化**二十一天。
indebted§He remained indebted to a teacher he never named.§他一直**感念**一位他从未提及名字的老师。
indecent§There was an indecent haste about the whole arrangement.§整个安排里有一种**不体面**的仓促。
indecision§Indecision is a decision that keeps its options and loses its chance.§**优柔寡断**是一种保留选项却失去机会的决定。
indecisive§The battle was indecisive and both sides claimed it.§这场战役**未分胜负**，双方都宣称赢了。
indecorous§It would be indecorous to mention the sum in public.§当众提起这个数目会很**失礼**。
indefatigable§Indefatigable is what we call people who never learn to stop.§我们把从不知道停下来的人称为**不知疲倦**。
indefensible§The position is indefensible and he defended it for years.§这个立场**站不住脚**，他却为它辩护了多年。
indefinite§An indefinite article is exactly what the sentence needs.§这个句子恰恰需要一个**不定冠词**。
indelible§Indelible ink was the whole point of the exercise.§用**不褪色**的墨水正是这次练习的要点。
indeterminate§The species is indeterminate from the fragment alone.§仅凭这块碎片**无法确定**物种。
indictment§The book is an indictment of a system it never names.§这本书是对一个它从未点名的制度的**控诉**。
indifference§Indifference wears the same face as patience.§**冷漠**与耐心长着同一副面孔。
indigence§Indigence is a condition; laziness is an accusation.§**贫困**是一种处境，懒惰是一项指控。
indigenous§Indigenous names survived the maps that tried to replace them.§**本土的**地名比试图取代它们的地图活得更久。
indignant§An indignant letter is best written and not sent.§**愤慨**的信最好写下来但不寄出。
indiscernible§The difference is indiscernible to the ear and obvious on paper.§这个差别耳朵**听不出**，写在纸上却一目了然。
indiscretion§A youthful indiscretion followed him into three elections.§年轻时的一次**轻率**跟着他经历了三次选举。
indiscriminate§Indiscriminate praise is a form of not paying attention.§**不加分辨**的赞美是一种不用心。
indisputable§It is indisputable that the wall predates the house.§这道墙早于这栋房子，这一点**无可争辩**。
